standard.title: Literary devices create character
standard.description: Explain the ways that literary devices and language features such as dialogue, and images are used to create character, and to influence emotions and opinions in different types of texts
standard.strand: Literature — Engaging with and responding to literature
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can identify and explain characteristics that define an author's individual style (AC9E6LE03). They have not yet examined how specific literary devices and language features — dialogue, imagery, description — work to construct character and influence the reader's emotional and evaluative response.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explain how literary devices and language features create character and influence emotions and opinions.

nodes.label: How literary devices construct character
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify literary devices and language features used to create character and explain how each constructs the reader's understanding of that character
nodes.minimum_width: In a given text, identify at least one literary device or language feature (e.g. dialogue, description, imagery) used to create a character; explain what it reveals about the character
nodes.typical_width: Examine how multiple devices and features work together to construct a character — dialogue that reveals personality, description that establishes appearance and setting, imagery that signals values or inner life — and explain how each contributes
wider: Compare the representation of a character's appearance in a novel and a film adaptation — how does the translation between modes (written description vs visual image) affect what is constructed about the character?
Examine how the absence of a literary device changes character construction — what would be lost if a character never spoke directly in dialogue?
nodes.hinge_reason: If students cannot explain how a device constructs character, Node 2's work on influencing emotions and opinions is inaccessible — both require the same explanatory move (device → effect on reader), and without it at the character level, students cannot extend it to emotional influence.

response_modes.reason: Students commonly identify that a device is present (there is dialogue) without explaining what the dialogue constructs (what does this dialogue reveal about who this character is?). The reasoning scaffold — device → what it shows → what the reader understands about the character — is the explanatory move this node develops.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one literary device or language feature used to create a character
Explains what the device reveals about the character

nodes.label: Influencing emotions and opinions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how literary devices and language features are used to influence the reader's emotional response and opinions in different text types
nodes.minimum_width: In a given text, identify a device or language feature used to influence the reader's emotions or opinions; explain how it produces that effect
nodes.typical_width: Examine how literary devices and language features influence emotional response and opinion across different text types — how imagery creates empathy in narrative, how dialogue reveals moral character in drama, how visual composition positions the viewer in film; explain the mechanisms of influence in each
wider: Explain the impact and significance of specific language features in a text — not just what they do locally but what they contribute to the reader's cumulative emotional and evaluative response
Compare how the same character is presented to influence the reader's sympathy differently in two different texts or adaptations — what devices are deployed to generate different emotional responses?

response_modes.reason: The mechanisms by which devices influence emotions and opinions vary significantly across text types — dialogue works differently in drama than in narrative; imagery operates differently in poetry than in film. Seeing the influence mechanism across genuinely different text types builds understanding of how influence is constructed, not just that it happens.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The comparison of novel and film representations of the same character is particularly rich — it makes the construction of emotional response visible by showing how different media use different devices to achieve similar or different effects.
success_criteria: Identifies a device or language feature used to influence emotions or opinions
Explains how it produces that effect on the reader or viewer
